Shorten the gradient one more grid step to test the fastest fully resolved method while keeping solvent window and temperature fixed. The first pair, now at R = 1.86, is the likely limiting pair; injection 9 remains a maximum-score fallback.

Test a four-minute gradient, lowering temperature another 5 C to compensate for compression of the first pair; the previous temperature decrease improved its R from 1.45 to 1.84. This seeks a faster maximum-score method, with injection 11 retained as the fully resolved fallback.

Test the minimum gradient duration at the lowest temperature, using the observed improvement in first-pair selectivity on cooling to counter gradient compression. Injection 12 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method if this two-minute gradient loses resolution.

This tests whether the first pair retains R ≥ 1.5 at the higher starting organic fraction; injection 14 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved fallback.

Shift the window upward another grid step while preserving the slope and temperature that gave full resolution in injection 15. The previous shift shortened the last retention time without harming the critical first pair, so this tests further acceleration while retaining CRF 1.000.

Continue shifting the solvent window upward at constant slope and temperature to shorten late-peak retention. The last two shifts preserved first-pair resolution near R = 1.6, making this a promising faster maximum-score method.

Raise the starting organic fraction one grid step while keeping the maximum endpoint and minimum gradient duration. This should shorten late-peak retention slightly and make the gradient shallower, but tests whether reduced initial retention compromises the first pair.

Seek a maximum-score alternative with better initial retention by lowering phi0 and temperature relative to injection 22. Its gradient slope matches injection 18, which achieved R = 1.77, while the lower starting fraction should move the earliest peak away from the dead-time region.

Raise injection 23’s temperature one grid step to shorten retention while retaining its safer initial retention window. Its first-pair R of 1.74 provides some margin for the selectivity loss on warming; injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.
